title: experimental-kernel-patch-triage-and-batching-checkins
content:
Context and purpose:
This doc captures the April week of ad-hoc triage and check-ins for the experimental kernel patch (low-latency attention rewrite), its interactions with the KV cache hot-path, and batching regressions we saw in canary. The goal is to record observations, decisions, risk assessment, and concrete action items for the next two sprints.

Attendees (04/14 sync):
- Evan Park (owner)
- Sofia Carter (benchmark lead)
- Priya N. (runtime engineer - kernels)
- Liam O'Neill (SRE, production rollout)
- Zoe Chen (infra - autoscaler & batching)

High-level summary:
- Canary for kernel-rewrite v0.9.2 exposed a 6–12% latency increase on short-context (<64 tokens) p50 in certain customer workloads due to an unexpected branch in the attention precompute path.
- The same patch reduced long-context (>2k tokens) throughput variance by ~18% and KV cache memory churn by ~10% across our internal stress tests.
- Batching anomalies: when combining the new kernel with our continuous-batching heuristics, p95 latency skewed upward under bursty request patterns; likely due to timer/flush interactions between kernel "early-complete" signaling and batch coalescing.

Detailed observations:
1) Short-context latency regression:
- Seen in canary: p50 delta +8% and p95 +4% on small chat prompts (~30 tokens).
- Root cause (initial hypothesis): the rewrite adds a lightweight mask normalization that executes even for short sequences; branch mispredictions on certain CPU/GPU drivers add overhead.
- Repro steps: run benchmark suite "chat-short-const-load" on g4dn.12x with batch size distribution matching SRV-1284; attach perf traces (see linked PR).

2) Long-context improvements:
- Throughput stability improved on sequence lengths >1024: less jitter in KV cache eviction and fewer full-cache re-materializations observed.
- Memory: observed 9–11% lower transient KV allocs in stress run (10k long-history chats) — likely due to reduced temporary buffer copies in the attention kernel.

3) Batching/coalescing interaction:
- When a request completes early within the kernel (early-complete flag), batching loop sometimes waits the full flush timeout instead of flushing immediately, increasing p95 under bursty arrival patterns.
- This effect is amplified when autoscaler introduces tiny instance churns (scale-up/scale-down) that change batch slot availability mid-window.

Risk assessment:
- Customer impact (high): Short chat latency regressions are visible for PLG customers on hosted API; unacceptable for SLAs if rolled wide.
- Stability (medium): Long-context customers see benefit; internal stability improved but not enough to offset short-context regressions without mitigation.
- Rollout risk (high): Without batching mitigation, canary to 25% might show increased p95s and trigger automated rollback.

Decisions made in sync:
- Hold broad rollout. Keep kernel v0.9.2 in limited canary (5% traffic) while we iterate on mitigations.
- Priority workstreams: (A) kernel micro-optimizations to avoid short-path branch, (B) batching loop fix to honor early-complete signalling, (C) telemetry to better attribute latency across stack layers.

Action items (owner — due):
- Priya: implement opt-out fast-path that bypasses the new mask-normalization for seq_length <= 128 and add unit tests (due 2026-04-19).
- Sofia: create detailed perf dashboard for short-vs-long context slices and add heatmap for branch mispred rates; attach baseline traces (due 2026-04-16).
- Zoe: modify batch flush loop to flush on early-complete flag and add guard to avoid extra flushes during instance-scale events (proposal PR by 2026-04-20, canary change 04/22).
- Liam: prepare a rollback playbook update (SRV-1284) that includes automatic remediation threshold tweaks and customer notification template (due 2026-04-18).
- Evan: coordinate a controlled canary expansion test matrix that isolates short-chat heavy traffic and long-context traffic to independent cohorts (test plan by 2026-04-17).

Short-term experiments planned:
- Experiment 1: kernel fast-path toggle (A/B) for short requests; measure p50/p95 and branch-mispred counters. Expected: recover <2% of p50.
- Experiment 2: batching flush on early-complete enabled in canary cohort only; measure p95 under bursty Poisson arrivals. Expected: reduce p95 skew by 10–15% without harming throughput.
- Experiment 3: KV cache aggressive pinning for long-context tests to verify memory stability under the new kernel; measure re-materialization events.

Notes on telemetry and observability gaps:
- We currently conflate kernel internal stalls with batching loop waits in the trace. Need to add a distinct trace span for "kernel-early-complete" and emit a short flag when kernel signals completion to the coalescer. (Linked Confluence doc contains suggested tracing schema.)
- Add histogram of seq_length at request ingress and attach to model-specific dashboards — several anomalies clustered around 56–80 tokens.

Blockers:
- Blocker A: lack of access to a matching GPU driver combo for one of our enterprise customers (they run a custom CUDA patch). Need validation infra. (Liam to follow up with support; created SRV-1299).
- Blocker B: small flakiness in perf harness causing noise in repeated runs; Sofia to stabilize harness (see linked artifacts).

Follow-ups / next sync:
- Quick triage standup Tues 04/20 10:00 PT to check on fast-path toggle results. Attendees: Priya, Sofia, Zoe, Evan.
- Full rollout review Fri 04/23 11:00 PT to decide canary expansion (if mitigations reduce short-context regression to <2% p50).

Freeform notes and TODOs (informal):
- Consider adding a lightweight compile flag to gate the normalization change so we can create specialized kernels for short vs long sequence models rather than runtime branching.
- Look into microbenchmark harness that simulates mixed PLG traffic patterns (mix of short chats + long-context retrieval) — current suites are biased.
- Keep communication ready for customer success: short note explaining why certain workloads benefit and others temporarily regress; pre-approved template in Confluence.

End of doc.
